name: Lee "Scratch" Perry
hook: Built a four-track studio in his back yard and got sounds out of it that 24-track rooms could not.
blurb: The Black Ark was a small studio behind Perry's house with only four tracks to record on. He got around the limit by bouncing recordings on top of each other over and over, which added hiss and smear every time. That damage became the sound, and engineers with better studios could not copy it and later spent decades trying to imitate it in software, which makes him the clearest case on this map of a limit producing a signature sound. He also recorded odd things on purpose, like rain, a cow, or himself breathing into the microphone. His production work put him directly into the story of English punk.

signatureTracks.title: Duppy Conqueror
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Produced for the Wailers years before the Black Ark existed, and proof Perry's ear predates the studio he became famous for.

signatureTracks.title: Police and Thieves
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Produced for Junior Murvin, and the record that carried dub into English punk a year later.

signatureTracks.title: Super Ape
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Perry's own name on the record, credited to the Upsetters, and the clearest Black Ark full-album statement of the murk he built out of a four-track's limitations.
